parts.note: a target is an object aimed at
a ball is round, a sphere

explanation.surface: A dartboard or archery target whose rings could be painted in any colour.
explanation.walkthrough: In snooker the ball you aim to pot with the cue ball is the object ball, and it may be any of the coloured balls, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: In snooker, the ball struck by the cue ball can be red or any coloured ball, so the target ball is any colour.

clue.text: Top removed from chimney-hoods to reveal hooters

indicators.note: the first letter is taken away from the word for these chimney covers

parts.note: cowls are hood-shaped covers fitted on chimneys

explanation.surface: Taking the caps off chimney-pots reveals birds nesting inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top removed from' takes the C off COWLS. 'Hooters' is slang for owls, from their call.
explanation.definitionFit: Owls hoot, so 'hooters' is a playful name for the birds.

parts.note: jet is a deep black colour, as in jet-black
a burn is a Scottish word for a stream

explanation.surface: Gales are blowing in the Lancashire town of Blackburn.
explanation.walkthrough: Blackburn is a town in Lancashire, but the word is split: BLACK gives JET and BURN, Scots for a brook, gives STREAM.
explanation.definitionFit: A jet stream is a fast current of air high in the atmosphere.

clue.text: Common bloke takes English to heart

indicators.note: the letter is taken into the middle of the word for a man

parts.note: a chap is a bloke, a man

explanation.surface: An ordinary man takes England's cause close to his heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Takes ... to heart' puts E in the middle of CHAP.
explanation.definitionFit: Something common or vulgar is cheap in the sense of low-class or tacky.

parts.note: to book is to record or enter, as a booking
let means allowed or permitted

explanation.surface: A short book produced from an approved record.
explanation.definitionFit: A booklet is a thin pamphlet-sized book, a small volume.

indicators.note: the letters are spread about and rearranged, like a soft cheese spread out

explanation.surface: Brie, spread thickly, is in generous supply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spread' reorders BRIE and ALL.
explanation.definitionFit: Liberal can mean generous or ample in amount, as in a liberal helping.

definitions.meaning: a cricket fielding position behind the batsman

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, slip is a close fielding position next to the wicketkeeper.
explanation.definitionFit: A slip is a minor mistake, and in cricket a fielder stands at slip beside the wicketkeeper.

clue.text: Citrus fruits left, half turned up

indicators.note: in a down clue the word for half is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: semi- means half, as in semicircle

explanation.surface: Citrus fruits, left behind, half of them upside down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned up' reverses SEMI to give IMES, after L.
explanation.definitionFit: Limes are small green citrus fruits.

clue.text: Bizarre Manet kept in safe-it has five feet!

indicators.note: the jumbled painter's name is placed inside the word for a safe

parts.note: peter is old criminal slang for a safe

indicators.note: something bizarre is odd and out of order, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A strange painting by Manet locked in a safe, whose subject has five feet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bizarre' turns MANET into NTAME, which 'kept in' puts inside PETER, criminal slang for a safe.
explanation.definitionFit: A pentameter is a line of verse with five metrical feet.

parts.note: AD (anno Domini) marks the present era, these days
an option is a choice

explanation.surface: Nowadays people take each other in their arms by preference.
explanation.definitionFit: Embracing an idea or child is taking it up as one's own, an act of taking on.

indicators.note: cut short at the tail, so the final letter goes

parts.note: to be in a lather is to be agitated

explanation.surface: The painter Turner's anxious state was cut short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turner' suggests the painter, but here it is a woodturner, whose machine is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A woodturner shapes wood on a rotating machine tool, so this tool is the turner's.

parts.note: grouse looks like the game bird but means a complaint: an official who hears complaints against public bodies

explanation.definitionFit: This official is appointed to investigate grievances against government bodies, a complaints adviser.

clue.text: Sunday drinker who produces dotty paintings

parts.note: a tippler is a habitual drinker

explanation.surface: A man who drinks on Sundays and paints eccentric pictures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dotty' looks like 'mad' but means made of dots.
explanation.definitionFit: Stippling is painting with small dots, so an artist using that technique produces dotted pictures.

parts.note: pa is dad, so pa's is dad's
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve

explanation.surface: Food served to the Home Guard in the TV sitcom Dad's Army.
explanation.walkthrough: Dad's Army is a British TV comedy about the Home Guard; here it splits into PA'S and TA.
explanation.definitionFit: Pasta is a food, and fare means food served.

definitions.meaning: a link by marriage, as in a relative by marriage
what you get when a phone call goes through to the other party

explanation.definitionFit: A relation by marriage is a family link, and a telephone call is put through as a link between lines.

parts.note: over means ended or finished

indicators.note: the letters of the drink are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Gorge yourself as the meal ends, before the tea break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Break' scrambles TEA into EAT, which follows OVER ('before'). The ellipsis links it to the previous clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To stuff oneself is to eat too much, to gorge.

clue.text: Put at risk in final wrath

parts.note: the end is the final part
wrath means anger

explanation.surface: Endangered by one last fit of fury.
explanation.definitionFit: To endanger is to expose to harm, to put in jeopardy.

indicators.note: the rules are broken and reassembled, letters jumbled

parts.note: ie (id est) means that is

explanation.surface: Fun that comes from breaking the rules.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Breaking' mixes IE with RULES.
explanation.definitionFit: Leisure is free time spent in recreation.

parts.note: issue means offspring: what a parent says when lifting a child who has fallen

explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation is said when lifting a small child, and issue means offspring.

indicators.note: spent as in used up and in disarray, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Monica spent the day roaming around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spent' rearranges D and MONICA.
explanation.definitionFit: Nomadic peoples roam about with no fixed home.

clue.text: Wad of notes found in the Savoy, for example

definitions.meaning: Savoy is a variety of crinkly green vegetable, not the London hotel

explanation.walkthrough: The Savoy suggests the famous London hotel, but a Savoy is a kind of cabbage.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang uses the leafy green vegetable for banknotes, and the Savoy is one variety of it.

indicators.note: the heraldic word holds the fashionable word inside it

parts.note: a fesse is a broad horizontal band across a shield in heraldry
in means fashionable

explanation.surface: A coat of arms with a band that holds a stylish skill at cards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contains' puts IN inside FESSE.
explanation.definitionFit: A finesse is a card-play technique in bridge, an attempt to win a trick with a lower card.

parts.note: F (forte) is the musical direction for loud
action means fighting or battle

explanation.surface: A noisy fight breaks out in the army camp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Camp' looks like an army base but means a side in a dispute.
explanation.definitionFit: A camp in a dispute is a group within a party, a breakaway side.

definitions.meaning: decent and without a criminal record
to char is to do housework, to scrub

explanation.definitionFit: Clean can mean decent or blameless, and a charwoman's work is to wash and scrub.

indicators.note: the letters are taken from inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Banish someone from Sussex in a hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'From' signals the answer inside SussEX PELl-mell.
explanation.definitionFit: To expel is to force out, to eject.

parts.note: to back is to support
a side is a team

explanation.surface: Backing the team, which is at the foot of the table.
explanation.definitionFit: Your backside is your bottom, the rear end.

clue.text: Hastings' last excursion to see the river

indicators.note: the final letter of the town's name is taken

parts.note: a tour is an excursion

explanation.surface: A last trip from Hastings to view a river.
explanation.walkthrough: Hastings is a seaside town in Sussex; the Stour is an English river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Stour is the name of several English rivers.

clue.text: We will get together shortly-in the spring?

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: will is cut to its contracted form, losing its first letters

parts.note: taken as written before shortening

explanation.surface: We will meet briefly in the springtime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get together shortly' joins WE and WILL as the contraction WE'LL. 'Spring' is a water source, not the season.
explanation.definitionFit: A spring is a natural water source, as is a hole dug to draw water.

clue.text: Showmen make mark endlessly with air-conditioning

indicators.note: the last letter is cut off the verb

parts.note: to impress is to make a mark on something

indicators.note: the letters are conditioned, reshaped into a new order

explanation.surface: Showmen make their mark by installing air-conditioning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endlessly' drops the final S of IMPRESS; 'conditioning' rearranges AIR as ARI.
explanation.definitionFit: Impresarios are theatrical producers and promoters, showbusiness managers.

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, O

indicators.note: the word for bad is read back to front

parts.note: evil means bad

explanation.surface: A sweetheart with a bad back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' reverses EVIL into LIVE after O.
explanation.definitionFit: Olive is a woman's name, so it denotes a lady.

parts.note: nil means zero
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: An athlete has run out of energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runner' is a river, as rivers run.
explanation.definitionFit: Crosswords call rivers runners since they flow, and this is the African river.

parts.note: p is the abbreviation for penny
royal means princely

explanation.surface: A stammered 'princely' suggests a regal plant.
explanation.walkthrough: P stands for penny in British money.
explanation.definitionFit: Pennyroyal is a mint herb.
